# Opero Docs

> Documentation for Opero product concepts, integrations, API tokens, and API workflows.

These docs describe public Opero concepts and the external Opero API. English is the primary index. Polish documentation is available under `https://kodasoft.pl/docs/pl`.

## Start Here

- [Welcome](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en): Overview of Opero docs and the recommended reading path.
- [Getting Started](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/getting-started): Find the API base URL, prepare an API token, and make a first request.

## API Essentials

- [API Overview](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api): Entry point for Opero API documentation.
- [Authentication](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/authentication): Use Opero API tokens with bearer authentication.
- [Language](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/language): Request localized API responses with the Accept-Language header.
- [OpenAPI](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/open-api): Use the current OpenAPI schema with API tools and client generators.

## Product Context

- [Opero](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/opero): Browse product documentation generated from public Opero documentation records.
- [Record Lists](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/opero/04-listy-rekordow/lista-rekordow): Record lists, list views, search, filtering, and export.
- [Automation](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/opero/07-automatyzacja/reguly-wprowadzenie): Automation rules, triggers, actions, notifications, and custom scripts.

## Extensions

- [Extensions](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions): Extensions add rule steps, triggers, data and screens to an Opero organization from an uploaded package, without deploying code.
- [Install an extension](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/install): Upload an extension package to Opero, review what it adds and what it can reach, install it and finish setting it up.
- [Run an installed extension](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/after-install): Check an installed Opero extension's health, complete its settings and connection, follow its schedules and runs, and decide what members can use.
- [Upgrade and uninstall](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/upgrade-and-uninstall): Review and install a new version of an Opero extension, confirm an upgrade that deletes data, and uninstall an extension with or without its data.
- [Before you start](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/before-you-start): What you need to build an Opero extension and to install it, how to get the opero-ext tool, and what an extension cannot do yet.
- [Tutorial: build Hello](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/tutorial/start-the-package): Scaffold the Hello extension with opero-ext init, read the manifest, the first action, its script and its test, and validate the package.
- [A step that only calculates](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/calculating-step): Build a small Opero extension with a Margin rule step written as a script, with no connection and no network access.
- [A package with its own data](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/own-data): Build an Opero extension that brings its own object, dictionary and saved query, and a step that reads and updates those records.
- [Forms, lists and pages](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/workspace-screens): Build an Opero extension that brings the screens members work with: forms on its own objects, Custom Lists and a workspace page.
- [Events from a service](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/scheduled-events): Build an Opero extension that reads a service every hour for each company and raises a trigger event that the organization's rules start on.
- [Data from each member's account](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/member-accounts): Build an Opero extension where each member connects their own account at a service, and a schedule brings each member's new data to the rules.
- [A block, a button and a link](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/blocks-and-actions): Build an Opero extension that members use on record pages: a block with a button, a record command, a link, and the permissions that guard them.
- [Start from your organization](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/start-from-your-organization): Turn configuration your organization already built into an extension package with opero-ext pull, finish it, and install it in another organization.
- [The package folder](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/package-folder): How an extension package folder is laid out, where each part goes, and the naming and YAML rules every file of the package follows.
- [extension.yaml](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/manifest): Reference for extension.yaml, the manifest of an extension package. Its identity, requirements, permissions and the lists of its parts.
- [Glossary](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/glossary): The words the Extensions pages use, and the names Opero gives to what an extension installs.
- [Command-line tool](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/cli): Install opero-ext, sign in, and look up every command with its options, consent, JSON output and exit codes.
- [Settings](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/settings): Give an extension values the administrator chooses, such as a region or a batch size, and read them in rule files, scripts and tests.
- [Connection and secrets](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/connection-and-secrets): Declare how an organization signs in to your service in connection.yaml, verify the credentials, and send secrets only where Opero allows them.
- [Member connections](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/member-connections): Let each member connect their own account at your service by OAuth with connection/member.yaml, and run actions with that member's token.
- [Objects](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/objects): Bring your own tables of records with object.yaml, with fields, references to the package's own objects and dictionaries, and the x-<key> module.
- [Dictionaries](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/dictionaries): Bring a fixed list of values, such as statuses, with dictionary.yaml, and use it in the select fields of the package's objects.
- [Queries](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/queries): Bring saved SQL queries over the package's own tables with query.yaml and a .sql file, and run them from SQL lists, reports, blocks and rules.
- [Data permissions](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/data-permissions): Ask for the data scopes your packaged rules need in permissions.data, and learn who can install such a package and when the scopes are checked.
- [Data steps](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/data-steps): Write the steps that read and write the package's records, run its queries, update contractors, send email and notifications, and generate documents.
- [Triggers](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/triggers): Declare a trigger with trigger.yaml so the organization's rules can start when something happens at your service, with its data, filters and dedupe.
- [Raising events](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/raising-events): Raise the events of the package's own triggers with the EMIT_EVENT step, with keys and dedupe so an unchanged item starts no rule twice.
- [Schedules](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/schedules): Run an action of the package on its own at a fixed interval with schedule.yaml, once for the installation, for each company or for each connected member.
- [Blocks](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/blocks): Show the package's data on record pages and custom pages with block.yaml, Liquid HTML, CSS, a script, buttons that run actions and render tests.
- [Forms, lists and pages](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/reference/screens): Bring the screens members work with, forms on the package's objects, Custom Lists and workspace pages, with form.yaml, list.yaml and page.yaml.
- [Error codes](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/extensions/error-codes): Look up any code from opero-ext, an upload, the install review, a run or a refused command, and find the page that explains it.

## API Resource Guides

- [Contractors](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/companies/get-companies-companyid-contractors): Work with contractors, suppliers, customers, and other business partners.
- [Service Catalog](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/companies/get-companies-companyid-service-catalog-items): Manage reusable services, goods, and bundles.
- [Custom Modules](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/custom-modules/list-custom-modules): List and manage custom module definitions.
- [Custom Objects](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/custom-objects/list-custom-objects): Work with custom object schemas and records.
- [Rules](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/rules/introduction): Manage and run Opero automation rules.
- [View Layout Configuration](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/view-layout-configuration/overview): Build and publish View Layouts for Opero records and forms.
- [View Layout Runtime](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/view-layout-runtime/runtime): Resolve published View Layouts, load runtime data, and save records.
- [Files](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/companies/post-companies-companyid-files-attachments): Upload attachment files.
- [Entity Attachments](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/companies/post-companies-companyid-entity-attachments): Attach files to Opero records.
- [Entity Comments](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/en/api/companies/get-companies-companyid-entity-comments-entitytype-entityid): Read and manage record comments.

## Machine-Readable References

- [OpenAPI schema](https://opero.kodasoft.pl/api/swagger/v1/json): Current external API contract.
- [Sitemap](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/sitemap.xml): Complete public docs URL list.
- [Search index](https://kodasoft.pl/docs/static.json): Public structured search index with page titles, descriptions, and content excerpts.
